tools.name: uk_stamp_duty_calculator
tools.description: Calculate UK stamp duty on a property purchase across England/Northern Ireland (SDLT), Scotland (LBTT) and Wales (LTT). Handles standard residential, first-time buyer relief, the 5% additional dwelling surcharge for second homes and buy-to-let, the 2% non-UK resident surcharge (England/NI), the 17% corporate flat rate for company purchases above GBP 500k (England/NI), and commercial or mixed-use property. Returns banded breakdown, total tax payable and effective rate. Uses current 2026 bands and surcharge rates. Calculated by Fox Davidson, whole of market UK mortgage brokers authorised and regulated by the FCA (FRN 1056214). Use when a user asks about stamp duty, SDLT, LBTT, LTT, additional dwelling surcharge, ADS, first-time buyer relief, non-resident surcharge, or tax on a specific UK property purchase.

property_price_gbp.description: Property purchase price in pounds. Example: 750000.

region.description: Tax region. 'england' covers England and Northern Ireland (SDLT). 'scotland' uses LBTT. 'wales' uses LTT.

buyer_type.description: Buyer category. 'standard' is a main residence purchase. 'ftb' is first-time buyer (England/NI relief up to GBP 500k; Scotland FTB to GBP 175k; Wales has no FTB relief). 'additional' triggers the second-home surcharge. 'nonresident' adds the 2% non-UK resident surcharge (England/NI only). 'corporate' applies the 17% flat rate above GBP 500k (England/NI residential) or standard rates plus surcharge below threshold or in Scotland/Wales. 'commercial' uses non-residential bands.

annotations.title: UK Stamp Duty Calculator (SDLT / LBTT / LTT)

tools.name: fd_hnw_mortgage_qualification
tools.description: Check whether a UK mortgage applicant qualifies as a high net worth mortgage customer under the FCA high net worth definition. The test passes if annual net income is at least GBP 300,000 OR net assets are at least GBP 3,000,000. The net assets test INCLUDES primary residence equity (per the literal FCA glossary G2953 and UK lender practice) and INCLUDES pension by default. Supports single applicant or joint application. Returns verdict, per-applicant test breakdown, joint household aggregate (if joint), and a routing recommendation including the relevant UK private bank list. Calculated by Fox Davidson, whole of market UK mortgage brokers authorised and regulated by the FCA (FRN 1056214). Use when a user asks whether they qualify for a high net worth mortgage, about the FCA high net worth test, the GBP 300k income or GBP 3m net assets test, private bank mortgages, or large loans against assets.

annual_net_income_gbp.description: Annual net income in pounds. Includes salary, bonus, RSU vesting (taxed value), dividends, partnership profits, business profits, rental income, carried interest. Net of tax.

primary_residence_value_gbp.description: Gross value of primary residence in pounds.

primary_residence_mortgage_gbp.description: Outstanding mortgage on primary residence in pounds.

investment_properties_gbp.description: Gross value of investment properties (BTL, holiday let, etc.) in pounds.

investment_property_mortgages_gbp.description: Outstanding mortgages on investment properties in pounds.

business_equity_gbp.description: Your share of business equity value in pounds.

other_assets_gbp.description: Other valuable assets (art, classic cars, jewellery, hedge fund holdings) in pounds.

pension_value_gbp.description: Pension value (SIPP, SSAS, drawdown, workplace) in pounds.

material_unsecured_debts_gbp.description: Material unsecured debts in pounds. Small consumer debt and normal overdraft buffer do not move the GBP 3m test in practice and can be left at 0.

include_pension_in_test.description: Whether to include pension in the GBP 3m net assets calculation. UK lenders applying the FCA high net worth definition typically include pension. Set to false for the conservative view.

applicant_2.description: Optional. If provided, the tool runs the joint application test which returns each applicant individually plus a joint household aggregate. Most lenders apply the MCOB 3A test per individual customer.

annotations.title: HNW Mortgage Qualification (FCA high net worth definition)

tools.name: uk_bridging_loan_calculator
tools.description: Calculate the full cost of a UK bridging loan: total interest, arrangement and exit fees, valuation/legal/admin costs, gross facility, net advance, loan-to-value, total cost of finance and an indicative annualised cost. Supports rolled-up (compounding), retained (deducted upfront) and serviced (paid monthly) interest. Also runs the FCA high net worth check: on a regulated bridge, lenders will write terms up to 60 months for an applicant with annual net income of at least GBP 300,000 OR net assets of at least GBP 3,000,000, against the usual 12 months. Calculated by Fox Davidson, whole of market UK mortgage brokers authorised and regulated by the FCA (FRN 1056214). Use when a user asks what a bridging loan costs, about bridging interest (rolled-up, retained or serviced), bridging LTV, regulated vs unregulated bridging, or the maximum term on a regulated bridge.

property_value_gbp.description: Open market value of the security property in pounds.

existing_charges_gbp.description: Existing mortgages or loans the bridge will repay, in pounds.

additional_funds_gbp.description: Additional cash required beyond clearing existing charges, in pounds.

monthly_rate_pct.description: Monthly interest rate as a percentage, for example 0.75 for 0.75% per month.

interest_structure.description: 'rolled' compounds monthly and is paid at exit. 'retained' deducts the full term of interest from the advance upfront. 'serviced' is paid monthly. Retained and serviced cost the same; rolled-up costs more.

arrangement_fee_pct.description: Lender arrangement fee as a percentage of the loan.

add_arrangement_fee_to_loan.description: Whether the arrangement fee is financed into the gross loan (true) or paid separately in cash (false).

exit_fee_pct.description: Exit fee as a percentage, charged on redemption. Often 0.

exit_fee_on_gross.description: Whether the exit fee is charged on the gross loan (true) or the net loan (false).

legal_fees_gbp.description: Lender and borrower legal fees in pounds.

admin_fees_gbp.description: Admin and other fees in pounds.

regulated.description: True if the bridge is secured against a property the borrower lives in or intends to live in (regulated). False for investment or commercial security (unregulated).

annual_net_income_gbp.description: Optional. Borrower annual net income, used for the FCA high net worth term check. GBP 300,000 or more passes the income limb.

net_assets_gbp.description: Optional. Borrower net assets including main residence equity and pension, minus all debts, used for the FCA high net worth term check. GBP 3,000,000 or more passes the net assets limb.

annotations.title: UK Bridging Loan Calculator (with high net worth term check)

tools.name: bridging_cost_analyser
tools.description: Calculate the total cost of a UK bridging loan across rolled-up, retained, and serviced interest structures. Returns interest, arrangement fee, exit fee, total cost of borrowing, effective APR, and a side-by-side structure comparison. Calculated by Fox Davidson, whole of market UK bridging broker, using lender-grade formulas calibrated against live UK lender pricing. For loans £250,000 and above. Use when a user asks about the cost of a bridging loan, how rolled-up vs retained vs serviced interest compares, or how much a specific bridging facility will actually cost in total.

loan_amount_gbp.description: Gross loan amount in pounds. Minimum Fox Davidson bridging loan size is £250,000. Example: 500000.

monthly_interest_rate_pct.description: Monthly interest rate as a percentage. UK bridging rates in 2026 typically range 0.55% to 1.25% per month. Private bank rates from 0.30% per month available on HNW cases. Example: 0.85 for 0.85% per month.

term_months.description: Loan term in months. Regulated bridging usually runs to 12 months; lenders write up to 60 months for borrowers meeting the FCA high net worth definition. Example: 12.

arrangement_fee_pct.description: Lender arrangement fee as % of loan amount. Typical range 1% to 2%. Some specialist HNW deals run 0.5%. Example: 2 for 2%.

exit_fee_pct.description: Lender exit fee as % of loan amount. Not all lenders charge one. Where charged, typically 0.5% to 1%. Example: 0 for no exit fee, or 1 for 1%.

interest_structure.description: How interest is paid. 'rolled' = compounds monthly, paid in full at exit (most common on HNW bridging, removes monthly outflow). 'retained' = deducted from advance upfront (borrower receives less cash on day one). 'serviced' = paid monthly out of borrower cash flow (lowest total cost but requires monthly servicing capacity).

tools.name: development_appraisal
tools.description: Run a UK property development scheme viability appraisal. Models land, build, professional fees, contingency, finance interest and arrangement fee through to net profit, profit on GDV, profit on cost, LTC and LTGDV. Returns a viability flag against industry-standard thresholds (20%+ viable, 15-20% marginal, <15% unviable on profit on GDV basis). Calculated by Fox Davidson, whole of market UK development finance broker. Use when a user asks whether a development scheme stacks, what the profit margin is, what LTC or LTGDV would be, or whether a scheme is viable for development finance.

gdv_gbp.description: Gross Development Value: total anticipated sales value of the completed scheme. Use comparable sales evidence, not aspirational figures. Lenders commission their own GDV via RICS. Example: 2000000.

land_or_purchase_price_gbp.description: Land purchase price. Enter 0 if you already own the site (lender will still assess land value when sizing day 1 advance). Example: 400000.

build_cost_gbp.description: Total agreed construction cost. Should be contracted figure where possible. Example: 800000.

professional_fees_pct.description: Professional fees as % of build cost. Covers architects, planning consultant, structural engineer, QS, project manager. Standard 10%. Example: 10.

contingency_pct.description: Contingency as % of build cost. Standard 10%. Lenders may require 12-15% on conversions or complex sites. Omitting overstates profit. Example: 10.

loan_amount_gbp.description: Specific loan amount in £. Optional. If omitted, calculator uses ltc_pct of hard costs. Example: 960000.

ltc_pct.description: Loan-to-cost % (used only if loan_amount_gbp is not provided). Most lenders cap at 90%; first-time developers typically 75-80%. Example: 75.

finance_monthly_rate_pct.description: Development finance monthly interest rate. UK 2026 rates typically 0.70% to 0.95% per month. Example: 0.85.

finance_term_months.description: Total finance term in months (build period + sales/refinance period). Example: 18.

arrangement_fee_pct.description: Lender arrangement fee as % of loan. Standard 1.5% to 2%. Larger facilities (£5m+) often 1.0%. Example: 2.

tools.name: btl_stress_tester
tools.description: Run a UK buy-to-let ICR stress test. Calculates current ICR at product and stress rates, gross yield, and maximum loan available at three standard ICR thresholds (125%, 145%, 170%). Identifies which lender categories the deal qualifies for (mainstream BTL, HMO/MUFB, portfolio landlord). Ownership-aware: personal name uses 5.5% stress rate; limited company uses max of product rate or 5.5%. Calculated by Fox Davidson, whole of market UK property finance broker. Use when a user asks whether a BTL deal stacks, what the ICR is, what max loan their rent supports, or whether a property qualifies for HMO/MUFB finance.

monthly_rent_gbp.description: Gross monthly rent in pounds. Use total rent for HMO and MUFB (all rooms / units combined). Example: 2500.

loan_amount_gbp.description: Loan amount being assessed in pounds. Example: 300000.

product_rate_pct.description: Annual product (pay) rate as a percentage. The actual rate the borrower would pay. Example: 5.5 for 5.5% per year.

ownership.description: Borrower structure. 'personal' uses 5.5% stress rate (HMRC tax exposure makes higher cover required). 'ltd' uses max of product rate or 5.5% (limited company SPV borrower, lower stress rate often allowed).

tools.name: fd_lender_criteria_lookup
tools.description: Look up how named UK mortgage lenders treat a specific underwriting question: contractor day rate annualisation, limited company retained profit, one year of accounts, lenders that do not credit score, bonus and commission, foreign currency income, maximum income multiples, maximum age at end of term, and private bank thresholds. Returns each lender's published position with the conditions attached, from 40+ UK lenders. Lenders publish their own criteria but none publish the comparison. Sourced by Fox Davidson, whole of market UK mortgage brokers authorised and regulated by the FCA (FRN 1056214). Use when a user asks which lenders accept a type of income or circumstance.

topic.description: The underwriting question. contractor_day_rate: how a day rate is annualised. retained_profit: whether limited company profit is usable. one_year_accounts: whether a single year of trading is accepted. no_credit_scoring: lenders that underwrite manually. bonus_commission: how variable pay is treated. foreign_currency: haircuts on non-sterling income. income_multiples: maximum loan to income. max_age: maximum age at end of term. private_banks: minimum loan and thresholds.

lender.description: Optional. Filter to one lender. Partial names work, for example "natwest" or "suffolk".

max_rows.description: Optional. Maximum rows to return. Defaults to 12.

tools.name: fd_compare_lenders
tools.description: Compare two to six named UK mortgage lenders side by side across their published underwriting criteria, and flag the topics where they differ. Answers questions such as "how does Halifax compare with NatWest on contractor income and retained profit". Sourced by Fox Davidson, whole of market UK mortgage brokers authorised and regulated by the FCA (FRN 1056214).

lenders.description: Lender names to compare, two to six. Partial names work, for example "halifax", "natwest".

topics.description: Optional. Topics to compare on. Defaults to every topic where the named lenders appear.

annotations.title: Compare UK Mortgage Lenders Side by Side

tools.name: fd_contractor_day_rate
tools.description: Convert a UK contractor day rate into the assessed annual income each named lender would use, and the indicative borrowing that produces. Lenders annualise the same day rate over anything from 41 to 52 weeks, so an identical contract produces a materially different maximum loan depending on the lender. Returns the full spread, best and worst outcome, and flags lenders whose published minimums the contractor does not meet. Calculated by Fox Davidson, whole of market UK mortgage brokers authorised and regulated by the FCA (FRN 1056214).

day_rate_gbp.description: Contractor day rate in pounds, excluding VAT. Example: 600.

days_per_week.description: Contracted days per week. Defaults to 5.

income_multiple.description: Optional income multiple for the indicative borrowing figure. If omitted, uses 5.5x where assessed income is GBP 60,000 or more and 4.5x below that, in line with what Fox Davidson secures for clients.

annotations.title: Contractor Day Rate Mortgage Calculator (by lender)
